note: Measured colorant spectra that replace the drawn curves in optics.json (JBK-967, JBK-957). src/scripts/measured.js turns each entry into decadic optical density per 10 mm at the page's reference amount (c = 1); scripts/build_measured.mjs writes the 25 nm copies into optics.json. Two kinds. 'bands': Gaussian bands fitted to measured spectra of glasses of known composition and thickness, in absolute units, so c = 1 is a stated amount of the ion. 'digitised': a curve read off a published figure whose absorbance is in arbitrary units (the authors normalised each curve to 0..1 and give no thickness), so the shape is measured but the strength is not; c = 1 is scaled to keep the old curve's daylight lightness. Digitised by tracing the figure pixels (5 nm steps, about ±0.01 in the normalised units).

cobalt.figure: Fig. 2, group B1: blue pot-coloured panes, soda-rich glass, 19th century
cobalt.sample: Stained glass panes from Panel 54/55, Abbey of the Dunes museum, Koksijde. Thickness not reported; relative (fibre) measurement without an integrating sphere.

background.why: The panes carry iron as well as cobalt. Co²⁺ is clear below 470 nm and above 710 nm, so iron's measured band shapes (Volotinen 2007) are fitted there and taken away; what is left is cobalt's.

chromium.figure: Fig. 3, group G1: green pot-coloured panes, 19th century
chromium.sample: Same panels. Chromium in both valences: Cr⁶⁺ makes the band near 370 nm, Cr³⁺ the shoulder near 450 nm and the band at 630–690 nm with its narrow dips at 633 and 682 nm. Thickness not reported.

silver-colloid.sample: Silver nanoparticles grown in the glass surface by firing a silver stain (radius about 2–6 nm by the authors' estimate). The figure ends at 650 nm; the last value is held to 780 nm.

iron-ferrous.table: Table 5.4.1: Fe²⁺ in octahedral and tetrahedral sites, with its ultraviolet peak
iron-ferrous.sample: 15Na₂O·15CaO·70SiO₂ (mol%) glasses melted in an electric furnace with up to 0.5 mol% Fe₂O₃, cast 1 cm thick; reflection loss and host-glass background removed.
iron-ferrous.unit: decadic absorbance per cm per mol% Fe²⁺

iron-ferric.table: Tables 5.4.2 and 5.4.3: Fe³⁺ in octahedral and tetrahedral sites, with its ultraviolet peak
iron-ferric.unit: decadic absorbance per cm per mol% Fe³⁺

copper.sample: The same base glass doped with CuO, electric furnace.
copper.unit: decadic absorbance per cm per mol% Cu²⁺

bandForm: A(ν) = a·exp(−(ν − ν₀)² / 2σ²) with ν in cm⁻¹; each band is [ν₀, σ, a]. Volotinen's 'width' is σ in this formula: with it, her Fe³⁺ bands sum to her stated 1.19 (cm·mol%)⁻¹ at 380 nm.
